custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a tracked part, part A, for this test at a cost of $10.00 and a Sell Price of $20.00, with 5 in bin location A and 0 in bin location B, so the report has two bins to add up.
    • How to do it: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Type ZZAUTOTEST PL C425660 PART A in Description and ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425660-A in Part Number, pick any category under Category, type 10.00 in Cost and 20.00 in Sell Price, type 5 in the Quantity of the bin row, click Add Bin Location, pick a second bin location in the new row and type 0 in its Quantity, click Default on that second row, then click Save.
  • Add 2 of part A to a work order line from bin location B while it holds 0, so bin location B goes to -2 and part A's net is 3 (5 + (-2)).
    • How to do it: Click Work Orders in the top bar, then Create Work Order; pick any Customer and any Asset, then click Save. The New Line window opens by itself: type ZZAUTOTEST PL C425660 LINE 1 in Title and press Tab, pick any Labor Rate, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the work order's Lines tab, in the line's Parts row click + Add Part, type ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425660-A in Part number, pick the result that shows Inventory Qty, type 2 in Qty *, then click Save.
  • Start on the Inventory Value report (Reports in the top bar, then Inventory Value under PARTS in the left menu), with the as-of date on today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report shows the test location only.

Step 2:

  • One row is listed for part A: Qty 3.00, Unit Cost $10.00 and Total Cost $30.00 (5 + (-2) = 3; 3 × $10.00 = $30.00).
  • Its Unit Sell is $20.00, Total Sell $60.00 (3 × $20.00) and Margin $30.00 ($60.00 − $30.00): every figure uses the net 3.
  • It does not show Qty 5.00 or Total Cost $50.00, the positive bin alone.
  • The Totals row reads Qty 3.00 and Total Cost $30.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, bug SV-10380 (Inventory Value report ignores negative bins and overstates net inventory value; ships with this epic)

  • Feature Overview, Accounting: “Inventory Value figures already saved for past dates keep their saved values. The count of bins below zero, which ships with this release, applies from release on and does not rework earlier dates.”

From: Product's answers (Chris Ward, 9 Oct and 14 Oct 2026, saved in po-answers-2026-10-09/ and po-answers-2026-10-14/), read 27 Oct 2026

  • QA lead, 9 Oct 2026, set-up answer 1: “Negative bin can be when you order the inventory part on a work order line when the quantity is already ZERO”

From: Jira tickets and comments under epic SV-10647 (saved in sources/jira-2026-10-27/ALL-TICKETS-2026-10-27.md), read 27 Oct 2026

  • SV-10380, description, Acceptance criteria: “At $10 unit cost, +5 and -2 bins produce quantity 3 and cost value $30.”
  • SV-10380, description, Reproduction table: “+5 and -2 | 5 / $50 | 3 / $30”
  • SV-10380, description, Expected behavior: “Use the net sum of all bin quantities, including negatives, for Inventory Value report quantities and valuation. Include negative-quantity parts with their signed values. A net-zero part contributes zero; this bug does not mandate displaying a zero-quantity row.”
  • SV-10380, description, Acceptance criteria: “Report rows, aggregate totals, exports and newly captured snapshots use the same net quantity basis for the same scope and cutoff. Quantity-dependent displayed values use that same basis.”
